title: Grateful Dead Live at Oregon State University on 1970-01-17
lineage: SBD > MR > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Good‑quality soundboard capture of a jam‑heavy winter ’70 show highlighted by an epic Dark Star/St. Stephen/Eleven sequence.
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard tape that sounds clearer than the room’s natural bass amp, with Jerry’s guitar front‑and‑center and only occasional hiss or song cuts. Musically the show shines – fans repeatedly cite the soaring Dark Star → St Stephen → The Eleven stretch, plus strong performances of Mason’s Children, High Time and Me & My Uncle, while Lovelight suffers a brief cut.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of the 20+ reviews are 4‑5 stars praising both performance and sound; only a few note minor issues (song cuts, tape speed), yielding an overall strong rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp guitar mix and natural bass amp give a clear front‑of‑stage feel; some reviewers note occasional hiss, a missing ~45 s segment of Lovelight, and a tape‑speed anomaly in one source, but overall the audio is listenable and better than an audience recording.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A well‑balanced winter ’70 set that blends mellow acoustic moments with long, exploratory jams; the second set builds to a powerful Dark Star → St. Stephen → The Eleven climax before closing on Lovelight.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is described as “nicely out front,” “perfect tone,” likely an SG, and drives the extended jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass gets a shout‑out for a simultaneous launch with Jerry during the Feelin’ Groovy jam, indicating solid low‑end support.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pig (Tom Constanten) is praised for his organ/keyboard work – even a borrowed church organ adds unique texture; some confusion about his status later in the tour.
